mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about trade barriers is NOT correct?

options.A: Tariffs increase the price of imported goods, protecting domestic producers.
options.B: Quotas limit the quantity of a particular good that can be imported.
options.C: Subsidies to exporters are a form of trade barrier that makes foreign goods cheaper.
options.D: Non‑tariff barriers such as stringent standards can restrict imports without raising tariffs.

mcqs.answer: Subsidies to exporters are a form of trade barrier that makes foreign goods cheaper.
mcqs.explanation: Subsidies to exporters are not a barrier; they actually encourage exports by making them cheaper abroad. Tariffs, quotas, and non‑tariff barriers are all mechanisms that restrict imports. Therefore option C is the misconception.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain the role of the World Trade Organization
mcqs.question: How does the World Trade Organization (WTO) primarily help reduce trade and investment barriers among member countries?

options.A: By imposing uniform tariffs on all goods traded between members.
options.B: By providing a forum for negotiating trade agreements and settling disputes.
options.C: By mandating that all members adopt a single currency for trade.
options.D: By directly subsidising the export industries of developing nations.

mcqs.answer: By providing a forum for negotiating trade agreements and settling disputes.
mcqs.explanation: The WTO's core functions are to facilitate negotiations (e.g., the Doha Round) and to resolve trade disputes through its Dispute Settlement Body. It does not set uniform tariffs, enforce a single currency, or provide subsidies. Hence option B correctly describes its role in reducing barriers.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand changes in India's trade policy
mcqs.question: Which statement best compares India's trade policy before 1991 with the policy after the 1991 liberalisation reforms?

options.A: Before 1991 India maintained high import tariffs and quantitative restrictions; after 1991 it reduced tariffs and removed many quantitative restrictions.
options.B: Before 1991 India had a completely free‑trade regime; after 1991 it introduced high protective tariffs.
options.C: Both before and after 1991, India kept the same tariff rates but increased export subsidies after 1991.
options.D: Before 1991 India was a member of the WTO; after 1991 it withdrew to protect domestic industries.

mcqs.answer: Before 1991 India maintained high import tariffs and quantitative restrictions; after 1991 it reduced tariffs and removed many quantitative restrictions.
mcqs.explanation: The 1991 reforms marked a shift from a protectionist regime (high tariffs, quotas, licensing) to a more open trade policy with lower tariffs and fewer quantitative restrictions. Options B, C, and D are factually incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Analyse effects on Indian producers and consumers
mcqs.question: After liberalisation reduced import duties on electronic goods, which of the following effects is most likely for Indian producers and consumers?

options.A: Producers of electronic goods will experience higher profits, while consumers will face higher prices.
options.B: Producers will face increased competition leading to pressure on margins, while consumers benefit from lower prices and greater variety.
options.C: Both producers and consumers will see a rise in prices due to increased demand for imports.
options.D: Producers will be unaffected, but consumers will have fewer choices because imports are restricted.

mcqs.answer: Producers will face increased competition leading to pressure on margins, while consumers benefit from lower prices and greater variety.
mcqs.explanation: Lower import duties make foreign electronic goods cheaper, intensifying competition for domestic manufacturers, which can compress their profit margins. At the same time, consumers enjoy lower prices and a wider range of products. Options A, C, and D contradict these outcomes.

mcqs.question: What does the term 'liberalisation' refer to in the context of India's economy?

options.A: The introduction of strict price controls on essential commodities.
options.B: The removal or reduction of government restrictions on trade, investment and industry.
options.C: The nationalisation of all private enterprises.
options.D: The implementation of a centrally planned economy.

mcqs.answer: The removal or reduction of government restrictions on trade, investment and industry.
mcqs.explanation: Liberalisation means opening up the economy by easing controls on imports, exports, foreign investment and industrial licensing. It does not involve price controls, nationalisation, or a centrally planned system.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a non‑tariff barrier?

options.B: A quota limiting the import of automobiles to 10,000 units per year.
options.C: Stringent sanitary and phytosanitary standards for imported food items.
options.D: A subsidy given to domestic textile manufacturers.

mcqs.answer: Stringent sanitary and phytosanitary standards for imported food items.
mcqs.explanation: Non‑tariff barriers are measures other than tariffs that restrict trade, such as technical standards, licensing, or sanitary regulations. Option C fits this definition. Option A is a tariff, B is a quota (still a quantitative restriction but considered a tariff‑like barrier), and D is a subsidy, not a barrier.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain the role of the World Trade Organization
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the WTO and distinguishes it from a free‑trade agreement (FTA)?

options.A: The WTO is a global organization that sets binding rules for all members, whereas an FTA is a pact between two or more countries that applies only to the signatories.
options.B: The WTO negotiates bilateral trade deals, while an FTA creates worldwide trade rules.
options.C: The WTO provides financial aid to developing countries, whereas an FTA imposes tariffs on all goods.
options.D: The WTO only deals with agricultural products, while an FTA covers services and intellectual property.

mcqs.answer: The WTO is a global organization that sets binding rules for all members, whereas an FTA is a pact between two or more countries that applies only to the signatories.
mcqs.explanation: The WTO establishes a multilateral framework governing trade for all its members, ensuring non‑discrimination (most‑favoured‑nation principle). An FTA is a regional or bilateral agreement that offers preferential treatment only among its participants. Options B, C, and D misrepresent the WTO's functions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand changes in India's trade policy
mcqs.question: If the Indian government decides to lower the import duty on solar panels from 30% to 5%, which of the following outcomes is most consistent with the post‑1991 trade‑policy direction?

options.A: Domestic solar panel manufacturers will receive higher subsidies to offset the lower duty.
options.B: The market will likely see an influx of cheaper imported panels, encouraging competition and potentially lowering prices for consumers.
options.C: India will ban the export of solar panels to protect domestic supply.
options.D: The change will have no effect because all solar panels are produced locally.

mcqs.answer: The market will likely see an influx of cheaper imported panels, encouraging competition and potentially lowering prices for consumers.
mcqs.explanation: Reducing import duties aligns with liberalisation goals: it makes imports cheaper, increases competition, and benefits consumers through lower prices and more choices. Options A, C, and D contradict the liberalisation approach.
